ask: C11, Linux, epoll, single-threaded event loop. server.c: non-blocking TCP server, epoll edge-triggered, per-connection growable buffer, line-delimited protocol, partial write handling with an output queue, accept loop draining EAGAIN, idle timeout sweep, SIGINT shutdown. main takes a port. write the file.
prose:
`server.c` is written — 17,804 bytes. Build and run:

```
cc -std=c11 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -o server server.c
./server 8080
```

The server is a single-threaded epoll edge-triggered event loop. Each connection gets a growable input buffer (compacts dead space at the front before reallocating) and a growable output buffer for partial writes. When `write()` returns `EAGAIN`, `EPOLLOUT` is armed via `EPOLL_CTL_MOD` and disarmed once the outbuf drains. The accept loop calls `accept4` in a tight loop until `EAGAIN`, which is required for edge-triggered mode. The line protocol splits on `\n`, strips trailing `\r`, and echoes back — replace `handle_line` with your real handler. Idle connections are swept every 15 seconds via `SIGALRM`, closing anything idle over 60 seconds. `SIGINT` sets a flag that the event loop checks, then drains and closes all connections before exit. `SIGPIPE` is ignored so a closed peer doesn't kill the process.
